text: This is the page the Sales Director actually opens first, three KPI cards, one trend line, one plain-language callout, built exactly to the wireframe from the planning lesson.

Three Card visuals sit at the top, bound to Active Customers, Churned Customers, and Churn Rate. Conditional formatting on the Churn Rate card gives an at-a-glance severity signal, green under three percent, amber three to six, red above, without anyone needing to know what the number should look like. A line chart adds the trailing-twelve-month trend, so a single snapshot doesn't get over-read as a change in direction.
The callout isn't a static text box, it's a DAX measure using TOPN to pull the highest-churn region straight from the model, so the sentence can't drift out of sync with the data behind it.
If a visual doesn't fit one of those four elements, it belongs on the drill-down page, not here. Re-run the five-second test once it's built, ideally with a different coworker looking at it cold.
Four elements, nothing more. Next: building that drill-down page itself.
